headline: In New Orleans, Carnival eats February and the Pelicans fit in around it
summary: The Pelicans fan year runs on low expectations and high loyalty: 26-56 last season, a new coach and no 2026 first-round pick. Interest peaks from late October through December. Then Carnival takes January and February, and Jazz Fest, crawfish and hurricane season take the rest. Fans buy culture first and team second, so the best retail moments meet Mardi Gras, second lines or Essence weekend.

insights.title: Carnival is the real February
insights.detail: Carnival season starts January 6, and Mardi Gras Day is February 9, 2027. The trade deadline (Feb 11) and All-Star weekend (Feb 19-21) land right on the post-Carnival hangover. Parade routes, school closures and the krewe calendar rule. Pelicans games compete with Endymion, Bacchus and Zulu weekends.
insights.implication: Don't launch a Pelicans hero drop in the two weeks before Mardi Gras. Instead, run Carnival-adjacent product (purple, green and gold throwback energy, throw-style graphics) as a January pre-sale that can bridge to the team.

insights.title: Saints Sundays and LSU Saturdays own the fall
insights.detail: Saints games and LSU football in Baton Rouge fill September through early January. The Pelicans opener (at home against Indiana on Oct 21, a day after the league tips off) and the November Cup nights compete with football. Casual fans tune in more once the Saints season ends in January.
insights.implication: Time drops to Friday Cup nights and weekday evenings, and don't fight Sunday. Co-brand around Gulf South pride, not Saints marks. The Saints and Pelicans share an owner, so check licensing and the relationship before any joint story.

insights.title: Cup group play is the early hook
insights.detail: The Pelicans are in NBA Cup West Group B with OKC, Minnesota, the Clippers and Memphis, opening Oct 30 at the Clippers. Cup games land on Fridays. Memphis is the nearest regional rivalry on the schedule.
insights.implication: Use Cup nights for a limited Cup-colorway or Friday-night capsule. A Memphis game is the natural Gulf South and Mississippi River story for a regional graphic.

insights.title: Hope follows players, not results
insights.detail: Two straight sub-30-win seasons have fans attaching to individuals: Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III (who survived June trade rumors), and second-year players Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears. A new coach adds a fresh-start story in October.
insights.implication: Lead with player product: Murphy and Zion signature or player-edition apparel, and youth sizing for Queen and Fears. Treat playoff gear as an upside scenario only.

insights.title: Spring belongs to the city
insights.detail: If the team misses the playoffs again, April and May belong to Jazz Fest (late April to early May), crawfish boils and festival season, and the Pelicans nearly vanish. The draft lottery and a possible high pick bring back some interest.
insights.implication: Treat April and May as a non-basketball window. Sell lightweight festival-ready apparel, and show up with Nike Basketball on neighborhood courts and in brass-band culture, not with Pelicans performance gear.

insights.title: Summer is hot and full of visitors
insights.detail: June to September means heat, afternoon storms and hurricane season. Essence Festival, around July 4, brings a huge influx of Black visitors and national culture to the Superdome and Smoothie King Center area. Southern Decadence at Labor Day draws another tourist wave.
insights.implication: Essence weekend is the best summer moment for retail and a collaboration with Black-owned creators. Pelicans product sold to visitors has to read as New Orleans, not generic NBA.

The dancing crowd behind a brass-band parade. It's a community ritual, not a style.
Beads and trinkets tossed from Carnival floats.

designCues.cue: Navy, Pelicans gold and red from the franchise palette
designCues.use: Make it the Association and Icon base, with gold #85714D and red #C8102E for trims and accents.

designCues.source: Mardi Gras traditional colors (justice, faith, power)
designCues.use: Pair with green #2E7D32 and gold #F2B705 for Carnival-season capsule pieces. Use it as a color story, not as parade-krewe imagery.

designCues.source: New Orleans civic symbol (also used by the Saints; Pelicans use it in brand marks)
designCues.use: Use the civic form as a small secondary mark or woven detail. Check Saints licensing before any prominent use.
Use tonal jacquard or laser-cut panels on warm-up jackets and hoodies.

designCues.cue: Pastel shotgun-house and corner-store color stack
designCues.source: Neighborhood house paint in the Seventh Ward, Bywater and Mid-City
designCues.use: Use as a softer secondary palette for lifestyle and spring-summer pieces.

designCues.cue: Hand-painted sign and second-line banner lettering
designCues.source: Social Aid and Pleasure Club banners and corner-store signs
designCues.use: Commission lettering from local sign painters, and credit and pay them.

designCues.source: Hot, wet climate and long outdoor festival days
designCues.use: Use mesh, quick-dry and linen-feel blends for shorts, shooting shirts and festival-ready layers.

productHooks: Carnival-season pre-sale capsule (Jan 6 to Feb 9) in purple, green and gold, built with a New Orleans creator and sold in the arena store and locally.
Cup Night Friday capsule keyed to the Oct 30 to Nov 27 group-play schedule, with a Memphis rivalry graphic.
Player-edition tees and hoodies for Trey Murphy III and Zion Williamson, plus youth sizing for Queen and Fears.
Essence-weekend collaboration with Black New Orleans artists and designers around July 4, with a share of proceeds going to a local court or youth program.
Heat-ready spring and summer line: mesh shooting shirts and lightweight shorts for April to September.
watchouts: Mardi Gras Indian suits, beadwork and feathers are sacred community art. Never copy them. Partner with Big Chiefs, tribes and Social Aid and Pleasure Clubs, and pay them.
Saints marks, the Who Dat phrase and the Superdome name are third-party IP. Shared ownership doesn't remove the need for a licensing check.
Don't over-promise playoff gear. The team won 26 games and sits in a low-expectation cycle.
Avoid Katrina-era imagery or rhetoric in marketing. It is lived trauma for many locals.
Avoid generic French Quarter and tourist iconography. Locals read it as outsider design.
